title: Analytics PII scrubbing and deletion workflow for Console usage pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement system-level PII scrubbing, retention enforcement, and data deletion controls across Console usage analytics pipelines. Goal is to provide auditable, automated deletion for user-requested DSRs, enforce per-customer retention windows, and remove accidental PII capture in event payloads before indexing or long-term storage. This touches event ingestion, enrichment, short-term stores, aggregated metrics, and S3/Parquet retention lifecycle. Must integrate with existing Console RBAC and audit log requirements.
acceptance_criteria: PII detection heuristics run on 100% of ingested Console events with <250ms added latency at edge path
Automated scrubbing removes or tokenizes detected PII fields and replaces them with consistent hashes or placeholders depending on retention policy

Deletion workflow supports per-customer deletion requests and returns a signed audit trail confirming data removed from: hotstores, long-term object storage, analytics materialized views, and third-party sinks
Retention policy enforcement job purges expired events nightly and emits per-customer retention metrics to the Console dashboard
End-to-end tests for detection, scrubbing, and deletion in CI with synthetic PII samples
Security review completed and documented; KMS keys used for hashing/tokenization are rotated and access-controlled
design_notes: Stage 1: Inline lightweight PII detector at ingestion (protobuf layer) that flags fields using regex + ML model for email/phone/credit-card/SSN patterns; default action = redact
Stage 2: Enrichment pipeline applies deterministic hashing for fields that need pseudonymization (email, user_id) using customer-scoped salt stored in KMS
Stage 3: Scrubbing rules stored in config (per-customer overrides): include allowlist/denylist of fields, retention windows, and sink exemptions

Deletion workflow: orchestrator triggers tombstone write to a deletion queue -> fan-out: delete from Kafka topic compacted store, run SS jobs to remove from Parquet blobs, update materialized views and invalidate caches
We will append deletion markers rather than immediate physical deletion for S3 objects older than 90 days and rely on lifecycle jobs to physically remove objects to avoid breaking analytical jobs
Audit trail: immutable append-only deletion log stored in an encrypted RDS table with FK to customer_id, request_id, operator, timestamp, affected datasets
To minimize downstream breakage, scrubbing will generate both a scrubbed event and a fingerprint index for re-joining to aggregated metrics when allowed by policy
implementation_plan: Add PII detection library and protobuf schema version bump; feature-flagged for canary customers
Create config service endpoints for per-customer scrubbing/retention rules and expose in Console UI (read-only for this migration)
Build deletion orchestrator service with idempotent workers and retry semantics; integrate with existing job queue (Ops)
Implement nightly retention purge job and S3 lifecycle policies coordinated with data team
Instrument metrics: scrubs/sec, false-positive rate (sampled), deletion latency, deletion success rate
Rollout: internal staging -> 5 pilot customers -> gradated ramp to all customers over 4 weeks
test_plan: Unit tests for regex/ML detector with positive/negative fixtures
Integration tests that simulate DSR: submit deletion request -> verify records removed from hotstore and parquet manifests updated
Load test ingestion pipeline with PII detector enabled to validate <250ms tail latency added
Fuzz tests for edge-case JSON payloads and nested fields
Backfill tests simulating historical data deletion affecting aggregated dashboards
Security fuzz/pen tests on deletion orchestrator endpoints
monitoring_and_alerts: Console dashboard: per-customer retention compliance (percent of customers with retention <= policy)
Alert: deletion-failure-rate > 1% over 1h -> page on-call infra engineer
Alert: detector false-positive ratio spike (sampled) -> create runbook to rollback config change
SLO: deletion request acknowledged within 10m, completed within 24h for datasets < 100M rows
Audit log integrity check nightly job; alert on missing tombstone chains
